title: Trees With the Same Leaves

concept.title: Collect the leaves in order and compare the lists
body: Two trees can have a very different shape and still carry the same **leaf sequence**: the values of their leaves read from left to right. To compare, collect the leaves of each tree with a depth-first walk that visits the left subtree before the right one, and compare the two lists.

In every depth-first order that goes left before right (pre-, in- or post-order), the leaves come out in the same left-to-right order, so any of them can be used. Comparing two lists is a plain equality check.

statement: The leaf sequence of a binary tree is the list of the values of its leaves (nodes without children) from left to right. Decide whether the two given trees have the same leaf sequence.
inputFormat: The first two lines describe the first tree and the next two lines describe the second tree. A tree is described by a line with the number of words `t`, and a line with the tree in level order (the root first, then the children row by row from left to right, `N` for a missing child, no `N` at the end).
constraints: The height of a tree is at most 800.

examples.note: Both trees have the leaves 6, 7, 4, 9, 8 in this order, although their shapes differ.

hints: Collect the leaf values of a tree into a list, visiting the left subtree before the right one.
The answer is yes when the two lists are equal.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root
